entries.title: Remarkable launches Forest Brown Leather Folio for the Paper Pure
entries.summary: The Remarkable Paper Pure now comes in a new classic Forest Brown leather color, designed for professionals, creatives, and design-conscious users. The post Remarkable launches Forest Brown Leather Folio for the Paper Pure first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Remarkable has just launched a new accessory: the Forest Brown Leather Folio for Remarkable Paper Pure. Crafted from leather in a timeless Forest Brown finish, this premium folio offers elegant wraparound protection while complementing Paper Pure’s minimalist design. Launching ahead of the peak gifting season, it provides a sophisticated upgrade for existing Paper Pure owners and the ideal premium finishing touch for new customers.

The exterior is made from genuine leather in brown and lined with blue microfiber padding, with magnets that wake and lock your device when you remove or insert it. Available as a standalone accessory or as part of a premium Paper Pure Bundle. The standalone Leather Sleeve Folio retails for $129 and is available now.

entries.title: The best mini e-readers of 2026
entries.summary: Many new small e-readers are already out or will be available soon; these are the best ones to spend your money on. The post The best mini e-readers of 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The best mini and pocket-sized e-readers of 2026 balance ultra-portable dimensions with sharp E Ink displays and flexible reading ecosystems. This is a really new product category that has only been picking up steam this year, and many entrants have entered the fray.

Xteink X4 Pro

  • The XTEINK X4 Pro is a highly portable, 4.3-inch pocket e-reader designed as a distraction-free alternative to smartphone doomscrolling. Reviewers from platforms like WIRED praise its featherlight 72-gram body and major hardware upgrades over previous iterations, most notably the addition of a responsive touchscreen and an integrated dual-tone front light with adjustable color temperatures for nighttime reading. To support these power-hungry additions, the manufacturer nearly doubled the battery capacity to 1,100 mAh while maintaining an ultra-thin 5.95 mm profile with built-in magnets for easy phone attachment. This device costs $99 on their website.

Onyx Boox Picco

  • The Onyx BOOX Picco is an ultra-compact, card-sized e-reader that marks a major departure from the brand’s usual Android tablets. Swapping Android for a custom, lightweight Linux-based operating system, this 3.97-inch pocket device ditches the Google Play Store to prioritize a distraction-free, hyper-portable reading experience. Early reviews from platforms like eWritable praise its featherlight 58-gram build and exceptional ergonomics, noting that its tactile, customizable page-turn rocker allows for effortless one-handed use. Unlike some miniature competitors, it includes an integrated adjustable front light that preserves screen depth and contrast, plus a convenient USB-C port and expandable microSD storage up to 2TB. It will retail for $109.99 when it comes out this Fall.

Pocketbook Q

  • PocketBook is launching its Q design e-reader this Fall. The phone-sized e-reader, with a 5.84-inch eye-safe, glare-free E Ink Carta 1300 touchscreen, is designed for everyday reading and listening to audiobooks. Physical side buttons make turning pages effortless with one hand, while the Linux-based platform keeps the experience focused on reading rather than notifications and endless scrolling. The product will be available in late fall for $235.00.

Metalio INK 4

  • The Metalio INK 4is a compact, 3.97-inch pocket-sized E-Ink e-reader and AI companion built with a premium 6mm aluminum alloy frame. It functions as a minimalist hardware device integrated with AI features like a built-in microphone, speaker, and camera, designed to let users sync data to the cloud and decouple from their smartphones. It connects over 4G or Wi-Fi, ships with Baiwen AI chat, a daily checklist, book reading, content transfer, and wallpaper push, and lets you flash the firmware directly from a browser. The device lacks an integrated frontlight for night reading and a gyroscope for automatic screen rotation.

It retails for $72.00 on AliExpress.

entries.title: Rakuten Kobo is now selling bundle sets
entries.summary: Rakuten Kobo now sells e-reader bundles that include a case, Kobo Remote, and 5 free e-books from Sarah J. Maas's ACOTAR series. The post Rakuten Kobo is now selling bundle sets first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Rakuten Kobo used to sell e-readers and accessories, such as cases and their Remote Bluetooth page-turner. The company has just started selling bundle sets on their website. They have various Libra Color bundles, Kobo Clara Color, and Kobo Clara BW. All come with five free e-books from the ACOTAR series by Sarah J. Maas.

The Kobo Libra Color bundle is very expensive. You get a Remote, 3 different color cases, and a Kobo Pencil 2. This bundle costs $399, while the e-reader on its own is $259. There are two bundles; the only difference is the e-reader color: black or white.  The Kobo Clara Color Bundle also comes in two colors and includes a case and the Kobo Remote; this bundle costs $239, while the e-reader alone is $179. The Kobo BW has the same bundle as the Clara color. However, the bundle price is $219, while the regular price is $159.

Most people who buy e-readers and have them out in the wild don’t normally buy cases. I see people all over Vancouver, BC, using Kindles on the SkyTrain, buses, or just out in public, and I can’t remember the last time I saw someone with a case. I suppose some people like cases so they don’t damage the display while carrying them in a crowded handbag, purse, or messenger bag.

Rakuten Kobo did not publicly announce the new bundle deals, along with the five free e-books, on social media, nor did it issue a press release.

entries.title: How to Listen to Kindle Books With CastReader
entries.summary: A practical guide to connecting your Kindle library on a phone or tablet and reading aloud in Kindle Cloud Reader on a computer. The post How to Listen to Kindle Books With CastReader first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
A practical guide to connecting your Kindle library on a phone or tablet and reading aloud in Kindle Cloud Reader on a computer.

You are three chapters into a Kindle book, but the rest of the evening involves making dinner rather than sitting down to read. Text to speech lets you listen to the same book, then return to the screen whenever you want to check a passage.

CastReader offers two routes. On an iPhone, iPad, Android phone or Android tablet, its mobile app can connect to your Kindle library and synchronize your bookshelf. On a computer, its browser extension works with Kindle Cloud Reader. The preparation differs, so start with the route that matches your device.

Choose the mobile app for phones and tablets, or the browser extension for Kindle Cloud Reader on a computer.

What Kindle text to speech can and cannot replace

A professionally produced audiobook includes a narrator’s interpretation of the writing. Text to speech generates spoken audio from readable text. It gives you a choice of voices and playback speeds, but not necessarily distinct performances for every character or an actor’s handling of unfamiliar names.

Neither format has to replace the other. An audiobook may be preferable for a particular performance; TTS is useful when you mainly want to continue reading. CastReader does not supply access to the book itself. You still need your own Amazon account and permission to read the title.

Before you begin

Choose a book that already opens normally in your Kindle reading service. Check a familiar chapter first, rather than discovering an account or access problem halfway through setting up narration. Availability can vary by book, account and region.

Use the mobile app on phones and tablets, or the Chrome or Edge extension on a computer. Installing a desktop extension is not a step you can simply repeat inside the Kindle mobile app. A familiar passage also makes it easier to notice missed lines or awkward page transitions.

Connect your Kindle bookshelf on a phone or tablet

Install the app. Visit the CastReader mobile app page and follow the link to the appropriate official app store. Open the installed app. Interface details can differ between platforms and releases, so follow the prompts in your version.

Connect your own Kindle library. Find Kindle among the reading services or bookshelf options and complete the account connection shown on screen. This brings your existing reading access into the workflow; it does not give other people access to your books.

Let the bookshelf synchronize and open a title. A cover appearing in the library is only the starting point. Open the book and check that the intended chapter displays correctly before starting narration.

Select Read Aloud and an available voice. Begin at a comfortable, ordinary speed. Listen to a few paragraphs before increasing it. Synchronized highlighting and automatic scrolling help you find the current passage when you want to look back at the text.

Check pause and resume before a longer session. The mobile workflow supports background listening, lock screen playback and resuming. Try these within one chapter first. Notice what happens when you leave the app, receive an interruption or change networks, rather than discovering the behavior during a long listening session.

For bedtime reading, check whether your version offers a sleep timer. It can prevent playback continuing far beyond the point where you fell asleep. These are CastReader reading controls, not a promise that every position will synchronize perfectly with all your Amazon devices.

Listen in Kindle Cloud Reader on a computer

Install the extension. Follow the Kindle browser listening guide to the official Chrome or Edge extension listing. Make sure the extension is enabled and has permission to work on the relevant reading page.

Open Kindle Cloud Reader. Go to read.amazon.com in your browser, sign in to your own Amazon account and open a book you can access there. Wait for the text to appear. If the book itself will not open, resolve that before troubleshooting narration.

Start CastReader and choose narration. Use the reading control on the page or the extension entry point, then select a voice and play. Button locations can change; the important check is whether CastReader recognizes the current page correctly.

Watch the first page transition. Listen to a few paragraphs and follow the move to the next page. If you hear repetition or a skipped passage, pause, find a clear starting point in the text and resume. Illustrated pages and extensive footnotes need more attention than straightforward prose.

The desktop workflow recognizes text from the visible reading page and sends the text needed for narration into the speech workflow. It is not a Kindle file downloader, exporter or protection removal tool. Continuous reading also depends on the accessibility and compatibility of the current page.

Make listening part of reading

Match your approach to the book. A familiar novel may work well alongside simple chores. A new story with many characters is easier to follow if you keep the text nearby initially. With nonfiction, pause at an important claim and look back at how the author supports it.

Maps, diagrams, poetry and dense footnotes are good reasons to switch back to the screen. Narration communicates words, not every relationship expressed by their layout. Moving between looking and listening is a useful reading habit; you do not have to stay away from the screen for the whole chapter.

Choose Read Aloud when you want the author’s text. Where supported, AI Explain can help you approach an unfamiliar argument, but its explanation reorganizes the material. It is not a substitute for the complete original or an exact quotation.

Understand the offline option

Current iOS release notes describe saving a Kindle book through the player’s More menu, finding it under Offline Books in settings and using a system voice for offline narration. That does not mean cloud AI voices or AI Explain work without an internet connection. It also does not establish equivalent offline support on Android or desktop.

Before a flight or unreliable connection, save the content in your installed version and test a short passage with the network disconnected. Confirm that the book, voice and reading position are available. A cached cover alone does not establish that you can listen offline.

Troubleshoot in a useful order

A book is missing. Check that you connected the correct account and can access the title in the original reading service. Then try the refresh or reconnection options available in the app.

The book opens but narration will not start. Wait for the body text to load and check the network and selected voice. On desktop, also check extension activation and permission for the current website.

Reading stops or repeats after a page turn. Find the point in the original text, pause and restart from there. Check for app or extension updates. Recent mobile updates include continuity, page transition and recovery fixes, but an individual book still needs testing.

A name sounds wrong. Check the language and voice, then try another voice or a more suitable speed. Return to the text if pronunciation affects your understanding; a generated reading is not an authority on how a name should sound.

Try your own book before choosing a plan

CastReader provides a free daily allowance. Pro expands access to standard narration and AI Explain. Website pricing is US$4.99 monthly or US$35.99 billed annually; app store pricing, region and taxes can differ. A subscription does not include the book’s purchase price or reading rights.

For occasional listening, the free option provides a starting point. Before subscribing for longer sessions, check whether your own book reads continuously, resumes reliably and sounds comfortable over a chapter. The aim is simple: give a book you already want to read another place in your day.

Markus lives in San Francisco, California and is the video game and audio expert on Good e-Reader! He has a huge interest in new e-readers and tablets, and gaming.

entries.title: Guide to Choosing an E-Reader in 2026
entries.summary: If you’re looking for a new e-reader, you may be wondering which one to get or which features are important. The post Guide to Choosing an E-Reader in 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
If you’re looking for a new e-reader, you may be wondering which one to get or which features are important. In this guide, we’ll discuss several popular e-reader options, features to consider, and how to find the right e-reader for your needs. We’ll also go through some other considerations, including choosing the right e-reader if you wear glasses.

Modern E-Reader Features

If you haven’t shopped for e-readers recently, you might be surprised at all the new features available. Here are just a few options that some of the latest e-readers offer:

  • External page-turning buttons or remotes
  • Waterproofing (great for reading by the pool or in the bathtub)
  • Increased battery life
  • Wireless charging
  • Improved contrast ratio for sharper pictures (nice if you read magazines or graphic novels)
  • Auto-adjusting brightness

I recommend figuring out which features are most important for your needs before you start looking for an e-reader. Some features may be essential to one person but inconsequential to another.

For instance, I’m used to turning pages on an e-reader and don’t really care about physical buttons. But several of my older relatives find the buttons hugely helpful, either because of mobility issues or unfamiliarity with technology.

Popular E-Readers for the 2026 Holiday Season

Here are some of the top e-readers to consider:

Amazon Kindle

Top features:

  • 6” display
  • 6-week battery life on one charge (on average, depending on usage)
  • Glare-free display with adjustable front light

This is the basic Kindle with the lowest price point. While it doesn’t have all the newest features, I know so many people who love them. They’re small and lightweight, so my friends who struggle with too-heavy bags or backpacks think they’re great. It’s also really easy to throw one in your purse or briefcase.

On the downside, it ships with 16GB of storage, and the Kindles aren’t designed for added storage. This isn’t typically a problem for people who tend to use Libby or other library apps where the book storage is temporary; they can just delete the titles they’ve finished. (In theory, you can do this with books you buy from the Kindle store as well, since they can always be re-downloaded, but that could be a hassle.) So if you feel the storage isn’t enough for your needs, you may want to consider another option.

Amazon Kindle Paperwhite

Top features:

  • 7” glare-free black-and-white display
  • Newest model is 20% faster
  • Comes with a free 3-month trial of Kindle Unlimited
  • Waterproof

Since the Paperwhite has the same 16GB of storage as the Kindle, its main advantages are a slightly larger size, faster speed, and the Kindle Unlimited trial. I actually think the trial is a good way to see if Unlimited will work for you. I got the trial with my Kindle Fire and found that most of the books I wanted to read weren’t on Unlimited, so I canceled it. However, I know other people who read on Unlimited frequently and find it a great value for the price.

If you prefer more storage, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition has 32GB and wireless charging.

Boox Palma 2 Pro

Top features:

  • 8 GB of internal storage, with the option to add 128GB of expandable storage via a microSD slot
  • Readable in direct sunlight
  • Compatible with Kindle books through the Kindle Reader app

Boox isn’t a brand that I’ve ever seen advertised in many places, but its name keeps coming up in e-reader or book forums. It’s a bit more oriented toward work and productivity than reading and recreation, but the Kindle compatibility makes it suitable for all of the above. If you think you’d like to use your e-reader for work or as a general Android device, Palma may be worthwhile.

I also find the Kaleido 3 color display interesting. It’s an e-ink system that’s intended to have a “newspaper-like” tone. At the same time, the screen doesn’t put out blue light like most backlit screens, so you can read it in direct sunlight.

If you’re packing for the beach or like to relax and read outdoors, this is a terrific feature. Throw your favorite UV protection sunglasses​ and this e-reader into a bag, and you’re ready for a relaxing day out in the sun!

Kobo Libra Colour

Top features:

  • Color screen
  • Ergonomic curve to fit hands comfortably
  • Annotate or highlight with Kobo Stylus 2 (sold separately)
  • Waterproof
  • Includes physical buttons for page-turning

The Libra Colour comes with 32GB of storage and an Instapaper feature for storing and reading online articles. It’s also compatible with the Kobo library, Libby, and most library apps.

The downside is that it’s not directly compatible with your Kindle library, which is discouraging for people who own a lot of Kindle books. You can convert Kindle files to work on Kobo with an app like Calibre, but this requires extra work that isn’t worth it for some people.

Choosing an E-Reader If You Wear Glasses

If you wear glasses, certain e-reader features can make reading more comfortable. Look for a device with an adjustable font size, a clear display, and lighting settings that let you customize the screen to your preferences.

The Kindle Paperwhite, for example, has a glare-free display, adjustable font sizes, and a front light that can be adjusted for different reading conditions. These features can be helpful if you wear glasses, especially when reading for extended periods.

It’s also worth keeping your glasses clean. Smudges and fingerprints can make text look less crisp and may make reading more tiring. Learn more in this article about glasses wipes.

What if I still struggle to read my e-reader with glasses?

If you prefer larger text, a device with a bigger screen may be worth considering. The Kobo Elipsa, for example, has a 10.3-inch display, giving you more screen space for larger text while still fitting more words on each page. You can also adjust the color temperature for a more comfortable reading experience at night.

If your e-reader is still difficult to read while wearing your regular glasses, reading glasses may be another option. Many retailers offer reading glasses in a variety of styles. For instance, on eyewear retailer EZContacts, you’ll find numerous options for stylish and affordable men’s and women’s reading glasses.

Markus lives in San Francisco, California and is the video game and audio expert on Good e-Reader! He has a huge interest in new e-readers and tablets, and gaming.

entries.title: New Kindle Scribe and Kindles have a new software update
entries.summary: The Kindle Scribe and all Kindles made after 2024 have received the 5.20.1 update, which adds microphone dictation. The post New Kindle Scribe and Kindles have a new software update first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The latest 3rd-generation Amazon Kindle Scribe e-notebooks have just received software update 5.20.1. This update was also pushed to all other Kindles made after 2024. Users on the Scribe can now dictate with a microphone: Use your voice to type in Kindle Scribe. Tap the microphone icon on the keyboard to dictate text in Search, book and document annotations, and notebook names.

Users can also now add handwritten sticky notes in fixed layout eBooks or personal documents. Use the sticky note tool in the writing toolbar or select text and use the action menu. Create a notebook to see the feature on the writing toolbar. Users are also saying that this update includes all of the Bluetooth drivers for the new Kindle Clip Bluetooth page-turner.

There are also the ubiquitous performance improvements, bug fixes, and other general enhancements.

entries.title: Pocketbook Announces the Verta and Verta Color
entries.summary: The Pocketbook Verta and Pocketbook Verta Color e-readers are very affordable and will be released soon. The post Pocketbook Announces the Verta and Verta Color first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Pocketbook is gearing up to announce two new e-readers, available in the next couple of months. They are the Verta with an E-Ink Carta 1300 e-paper display and the Verta Color; these two devices will replace the Verse and Verse Color.

The Verta features a 6-inch E Ink Carta 1300 display with a resolution of 1,448 x 1,072 pixels at 300 PPI, which can display only 16 shades of gray. The Verta Color instead uses an E Ink Kaleido 3 panel that can also display 4,096 colors. The black-and-white e-paper display is 300 PPI, and the color display is 150 PPI. Both models have both a front-lit display and warm lighting.

Under the hood is a Rockchip RK3566 Quad-core ARM Cortex-A55 CPU running at 1.8 GHz, 1 GB of RAM, and 16 GB of internal storage. Bluetooth 5.0 supports audiobooks, and you can buy e-books from the PocketBook Store. Libby is preinstalled, and users can browse their local branch to borrow e-books, audiobooks, and digital magazines. A USB-C port is for transferring content and charging. The e-readers are powered by a 1,500 mAh battery, which lasts a couple of weeks of heavy use. Both of these e-readers are waterproof and rated IPX4.

Supported e-book formats include ACSM, CHM, DJVU, DOC, DOCX, EPUB, EPUB(DRM), FB2, FB2.ZIP, HTM, HTML, MOBI, PDF, PDF (DRM), PRC, RTF, TXT, AZW, CBR, AZW3, and CBZ.

The Verta will be available in many back-plate colors, such as black, white, red, and yellow. These are sold separately. It will retail for $169 when it comes out soon. The Verta Color will cost $179.99. That makes these devices affordable and cheaper than current-generation Kindle e-readers.

entries.title: These are the Kindle e-readers on sale for Prime Big Deals Day
entries.summary: Amazon has several previous-generation Kindles on sale, along with the current-gen Kindle Scribe. The post These are the Kindle e-readers on sale for Prime Big Deals Day first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Looking for the best deals of the fall season? Prime Big Deal Days is Amazon’s annual two-day shopping event for Prime members, with exclusive savings across more than 35 categories—all with fast, free delivery. Looking for the best Kindle deals? Here is everything you need to know.

Amazon has put some of its previous-gen Kindles on sale ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, along with the Kindle Scribe and Kindle Scribe Colorsoft. Somehow, the Kindle Scribe without a front light still isn’t on sale, and it hasn’t gone on sale once since its release.

Amazon Kindle Colorsoft 16 GB (2024 model) – With color display that brings covers and content to...

  • Read in color – The 7" Colorsoft display is high-contrast and easy on the eyes, with paper-like color that brings covers and content to life.
  • A brand-new experience – The Kindle Colorsoft display is optimized for reading in color and is different from the Kindle Paperwhite display, which is optimized for black and white reading.
  • Color your pages – Highlight your favorite scenes in yellow, orange, blue, and pink.

Amazon Kindle Colorsoft Kids 16 GB (2024 model) – Lightweight, compact, and designed for...

  • Everything kids need to love reading – Includes 12 months of Amazon Kids+, a kid-friendly cover, and a 2-year worry-free guarantee – up to a $364 value.
  • The first Kindle in color for kids – The new Colorsoft display brings covers and content to life. Kids can explore titles included in their subscription, like Artemis Fowl, Big Nate, and Percy Jackson, in paper-like color that’s easy on the eyes.
  • Content kids love – Get unlimited access to thousands of age-appropriate books with 12 months of Amazon Kids+, an included subscription designed for kids aged 3-12. After 12 months, your subscription will automatically renew every month starting at just $7.99/month plus applicable tax. You may cancel at any time by visiting the Amazon Parent Dashboard or contacting Customer Service.

Amazon Kindle Paperwhite 16GB (2024 model) – 7" glare-free display and weeks of battery life...

  • Our fastest Kindle Paperwhite ever – The next-generation 7“ Paperwhite display has a higher contrast ratio and 25% faster page turns.
  • Ready for travel – The ultra-thin design has a larger glare-free screen so pages stay sharp no matter where you are.
  • Escape into your books – Your Kindle doesn’t have social media, notifications, or other distracting apps.

Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition 32GB (2024 model) – Auto-adjusting front light...

  • Our fastest Kindle Paperwhite ever – The next-generation 7“ Paperwhite display has a higher contrast ratio and 25% faster page turns.
  • Upgrade your reading experience – The Signature Edition features an auto-adjusting front light, wireless charging, and 32 GB storage.
  • Ready for travel – The ultra-thin design has a larger glare-free screen so pages stay sharp no matter where you are.

Amazon Kindle 16 GB (2024 model) - Light and compact, with fast page turns, and high contrast ratio...

  • Light and compact - With adjustable brightness, high contrast ratio, and fast page turns.
  • Effortless reading in any light - Read comfortably with a 6“ glare-free display, adjustable front light—now 25% brighter at max setting—and dark mode.
  • Escape into your books - Tune out messages, emails, and social media with a distraction-free reading experience.

Amazon Kindle Scribe Colorsoft 64GB (newest model) — 11” paper-like color display — Write in...

  • Our most advanced Kindle Scribe – Features an 11” Colorsoft display with front light, built-in notebook, AI tools, and support for popular cloud services.
  • Bring ideas to life in color – The custom-built Colorsoft display delivers high-contrast, paper-like color that’s easy on the eyes without distracting flashes when writing.
  • Get a pen-on-paper feel: The textured surface and responsive display create a smooth, paper-like writing experience. Plus, the included pen never needs charging and has a built-in eraser and shortcut button for tools like the highlighter.

Amazon Kindle Scribe 32GB (newest model) — 11” display with front light, paper-like feel, and no...

  • All-new Kindle Scribe – Features an 11” glare-free display with front light, built-in notebook, AI tools, and support for popular cloud services.
  • Get a pen-on-paper feel – The textured surface and responsive display create a smooth, paper-like writing experience. Plus, the included pen never needs charging and has a built-in eraser and shortcut button for tools like the highlighter.
  • More room to read, write, and think – At just 5.4mm thin and 400g light, it’s redesigned for comfort, with a larger 11" display and 40% faster writing and page turns.

entries.title: Top 10 New Audiobooks for October 2026
entries.summary: New audiobooks for October 2026 include major anticipated releases like Partita by Barbara Kingsolver and Peck & Peck by Bonnie Garmus. The post Top 10 New Audiobooks for October 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Bram Stoker’s Dracula, adapted by Robyn Ahern and narrated by a full cast including Ella Purnell and Jonathan Bailey, stands out as the top audiobook pick for October 2026.

Threshing Day (Wing and Claw Collection)

The Threshing Day audiobook by Rebecca Yarros—part of the Empyrean universe's Wing and Claw Collection—was officially released on September 29, 2026. This special release features 13 standalone stories centering around beloved Fourth Wing characters (such as Xaden, Rhiannon, Dain, Liam, and more) as they navigate the brutal, high-stakes dragon-bonding trial at Basgiath War College.

The French Illusion: A Novel

The French Illusion audiobook by John Grisham was released on September 29, 2026. Marking a major departure from his classic courtroom dramas, this high-stakes release is Grisham's first-ever pure espionage thriller. The plot follows an American couple kidnapped during their honeymoon in Paris, pulling a young lawyer into an elaborate cross-border CIA operation to catch the culprits.

The Steps: A Memoir

The Steps audiobook by Sylvester Stallone was officially released on September 29, 2026. This powerful autobiography is narrated by Sylvester Stallone himself and features exclusive, original background music composed by legendary Rocky composer Bill Conti.

Miss Wolcott's Ghost: A Novel

Miss Wolcott’s Ghost audiobook by Louise Penny. It is scheduled for release on October 20, 2026. In an exciting development for fans, this 21st installment in the Chief Inspector Armand Gamache series is narrated by Alfred Molina—the acclaimed actor who previously portrayed Gamache in the Three Pines television adaptation.

A Court of Splintered Harmony

The A Court of Splintered Harmony audiobook by Sarah J. Maas—the highly anticipated sixth book in the A Court of Thorns and Roses (ACOTAR) series—is officially scheduled for release on October 27, 2026.

Rules to Live By: How Extraordinary Lives Define What Really Matters

The Rules to Live By audiobook by professional climber, National Geographic photographer, and Academy Award–winning filmmaker Jimmy Chin was officially released on September 29, 2026.

Trust Fall

The Trust Fall audiobook by Lynn Painter was officially released on September 29, 2026. This rags-to-riches, opposites-attract romantic comedy is narrated by Saylor Bell Curda and Aidan Bissett.

Partita: A Novel

The Partita audiobook by Pulitzer Prize-winning author Barbara Kingsolver is officially scheduled for release tomorrow, October 6, 2026. This deeply moving novel is narrated by Megan Tusing.

Bram Stoker's Dracula

Audible presents Dracula, a brand-new, full-cast adaptation of Bram Stoker's masterpiece starring Ella Purnell, Jonathan Bailey, Aimee Lou Wood, Louis Partridge, David Jonsson, and Maggie Gyllenhaal.

entries.title: Pocketbook e-readers can now borrow magazines with Libby
entries.summary: A new software update for Pocketbook E-Readers has introduced digital magazine support for the Libby app. The post Pocketbook e-readers can now borrow magazines with Libby first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
PocketBook e-readers have had native Libby support for digital libraries. Users with newer models and older devices could browse their public library, borrow audiobooks and e-books, and read or listen to them on the PocketBook. The company just released the 6.11.1437 update, which now lets users borrow digital magazines through Libby-supported libraries.

The changelog states that “Magazines are now supported in the Libby app. Users can discover magazines in the library and search, borrow individual issues, and track what they’ve already checked out – all from a dedicated magazine page showing covers, issue details, and availability at a glance.”

Supported models include the Pocketbook Era, Pocketbook Verse Pro, and Pocketbook InkPad 4, along with existing models such as the Pocketbook Verse Pro Color, Pocketbook InkPad One, and Era Color. All of these e-readers are receiving the new software update.

The company also added automatic Bluetooth audio connection. The device now connects to a previously paired audio device automatically when it becomes available, when playback starts, or when Bluetooth is turned on, without any manual steps. If the connection drops, playback pauses and resumes automatically once reconnected, with a limited number of retry attempts.

Added the Send-to-Email feature to the Notepad application, allowing users to send notes directly from the device to one or multiple recipients, either as an attachment or in the email body, with PDF and TXT export options. Added an AI Selection function to the Notepad application, allowing users to simply circle handwritten text to instantly trigger handwriting recognition. They also added a Magic Shapes function to the Notepad application, automatically transforming rough hand-drawn circles, rectangles, arrows, and other shapes into clean geometric figures.

Bug fixes also include adjusting music or audiobook volume with headphone volume controls. Fixed an issue where audio playback did not resume correctly after the device automatically reconnected to Bluetooth headphones or a speaker.

Wrap up

Some e-readers let you borrow e-books from the public library. In the United States, you can visit your local branch’s website and use Send to Kindle. Kobo e-readers have OverDrive integration that only supports e-books, even though they all have an audiobook player; borrowing audiobooks is impossible.

Now that many PocketBook e-reader software platforms are mature enough, they are the only brand that supports e-books, audiobooks, and now digital magazines. Borrowing on a PocketBook is easy: simply attach your library card and four-digit PIN, and you can browse your local branch’s entire digital collection, borrow, and do everything on the e-reader without a computer or USB connection.
